To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) aphasic comprehension disorders reflect the disruption of syntactic processing capacities, (b) the syntactic processing capacities disrupted are capacities for the on-line, incremental processing of syntactic information, (c) the syntactic information that aphastics have difficulty processing is the information that is required for the on-line resolution of syntactic ambiguity, (d) this difficulty processing information that is required to resolve syntactic ambiguity is a reflection of a disruption of the capacity to process syntactic information incrementally,

(a) the syntactic limitations of aphasics reflect the breakdown of the processing resources that are used to construct syntactic representations; and (b) these processing resources are cortically localizable, and are located in the left hemisphere.

the comprehension of sentences with complex syntax is disrupted by lesions of the temporal cortex, whereas lesions of the frontal cortex are associated with comprehension disorders that are limited to sentences with simple syntax.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the neurological organization of a complex cognitive function (sentence comprehension), and we have found that the function is organized hierarchically and that the organization is reflected in the pattern of aphasic comprehension deficits.
the neurological organization of the comprehension of sentences.
the following question: How does the brain organize the comprehension of complex sentences?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neurological organization of the comprehension capacity is the same as the neurological organization of language production.
sentence comprehension capacity is organized by a set of functionally distinct and cortically localizable processes that are engaged by the syntactic structure of the sentences to be processed.
the comprehension of sentences with syntactic structure is a cortical function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aphasic disorders of sentence comprehension reflect the breakdown of syntactic processing resources.

the left frontal lobe is involved in syntactic processing (in particular, in the processing of syntactic structure) and that the temporal lobe is involved (in particular, the left temporal lobe) in lexical processing (in particular the processing of lexical-semantic information).
sentence comprehension capacity is organized in the brain in a way that reflects the organization of the sentence in the mind.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the comprehension of sentences is organized into a number of functionally distinct processes, each of which is supported by a specific set of processing resources, and each of which is subject to selective impairment in aphasia.
aphasic comprehension impairment is not a unitary disorder but rather a set of disorders that are associated with the disruption of different aspects of syntactic processing.
the syntactic limitations in sentence comprehension are due to a breakdown of the ability to access and manipulate the syntactic information in the sentence.
